title: Mind Control of LLMs via Closed-Loop Stimulation: Out-of-Distribution Robustness
abstract: arXiv:2611.06418v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Brains and large language models need not be considered equivalent systems to reveal an interpretable commonality: both exhibit high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamics whose behavior can only be modeled imperfectly. This creates a shared challenge whenever we seek to intervene in their dynamics. A controller may either rely on a model identified around a particular operating regime and risk failure as the system moves away from that regime, or explicitly account for uncertainty and a changing internal state. Neurostimulation has confronted an analogous problem for decades. The limitations of fixed, open-loop stimulation have motivated closed-loop and state-dependent approaches that condition intervention on the ongoing state of the neural system. translated_title: 通过闭环刺激实现大语言模型的“意念控制”：分布外鲁棒性
translated_abstract: 大脑和大语言模型不必被视为等价系统，也能揭示出一个可解释的共性：两者都表现出高维、非线性的动力学特性，其行为只能被不完美地建模。这在我们试图干预其动力学时带来了共同的挑战。控制器要么依赖于在特定工作点附近辨识出的模型，并承担系统偏离该工作点时失效的风险；要么显式地考虑不确定性和不断变化的内部状态。神经刺激领域几十年来一直面临类似的问题：固定开环刺激的局限性推动了闭环和状态依赖方法的发展，这些方法根据神经系统的实时状态来调节干预。受这一原则启发，我们将大语言模型引导表述为一个反馈控制问题，其中网络的内部状态——而非单一的固定干预——决定系统如何被扰动。
tldr: 受神经刺激领域闭环控制原理启发，本文将大语言模型引导表述为反馈控制问题，通过模型内部状态动态调节干预，从而在分布外场景下实现鲁棒的模型行为控制。
en_tdlr: Inspired by closed-loop neurostimulation, this paper formulates LLM steering as a feedback-control problem that conditions interventions on the model's internal state, achieving robust out-of-distribution control.
